children: Many Bank of Japan board members saw the need to focus on mounting inflation risks, with some calling for faster interest rate hikes, minutes of the bank's July meeting showed on Monday.

"Markets appeared to be expecting the BOJ to raise interest rates with intervals of about six months. But the pace of rate hikes could be faster than such market expectations, given underlying inflation had approached 2% and the greater need to focus on upside price risks," one member was quoted as saying.
